item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-f552bda379300032","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The UN human-rights office reported that Mexico transferred the Guardia Nacional's operational, budgetary, and administrative control to the exclusively military-led Secretaría de la Defensa Nacional, despite the force's constitutionally civil character. It warned that the reform consolidated military involvement in public security without effective civilian supervision, after militarization had not produced a sustainable reduction in crime and had coincided with increased allegations of serious human-rights violations; public participation and debate before approval were limited.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","4B.6","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The document concerns a 2022 decision and its implications, relevant as inherited policy context for AMLO's 2023 record rather than a 2023-only event.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the legislative transfer to Mexico's Congress and the broader militarization trend to Mexican authorities; it does not identify AMLO's personal act in this excerpt.","limitations":["No 2023 outcome data or documented corrective action is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-215bf555123d0930","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"ILO-linked studies found severe deprivation of labor and social protections among paid domestic workers: 99.2% lacked written contracts, 98.3% lacked access to health institutions, and 71.3% received no benefits. Women had markedly lower access than men to bonuses and paid leave; many workers earned below the minimum wage and worked more than 48 hours weekly. The studies identified ratification of ILO Convention 189, mandatory social security, regulated hours, sectoral wages, and employer inspection as needed reforms, noting Mexico had not ratified the convention at the time of publication.","question_ids":["5B.8","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.8","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published in 2019, so it establishes a pre-2023 structural baseline and does not demonstrate AMLO's 2023 policy response.","ruler_attribution":"The source reports national conditions and recommends government, worker, and employer action; it does not attribute the conditions or non-ratification personally to AMLO.","limitations":["No 2023 implementation, ratification, budget, or outcome evidence is provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b779baec24c1333b","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL's 2022 social-policy evaluation reported advances in social-rights exercise and in applying rights and life-course perspectives, but also identified growing gaps and inequalities affecting groups including Indigenous people, program gaps, and a lack of integrated vision. It documented actions addressing most life-course risks while recommending further measures to guarantee social rights and strengthen policy.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report covers 2018-2022 and provides baseline and near-period evidence for assessing 2023, not a direct 2023 result.","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates federal social policy during the period but does not assign each finding or recommendation personally to AMLO.","limitations":["The supplied page summarizes the report without program-level causal estimates or 2023 follow-up."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0b1b38fdcb022f70","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"In Mexico's October 2023 UN First Committee statement, the government rejected all weapons of mass destruction and their use under any circumstances, urged universalization of the Chemical Weapons Convention, supported stronger verification for the Biological Weapons Convention, highlighted catastrophic dual-use risks in synthetic biology, biotechnology, biogenetics, and research, and called for stronger biological-material controls and analysis of emerging technologies through the Security Council 1540 Committee.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.4","1B.6","1B.7","1B.9","1B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly dated to 17 October 2023 and therefore fits the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The statement is formally delivered by Mexico; it is evidence of the administration's official international position, though the excerpt does not document AMLO's personal drafting or implementation decisions.","limitations":["It records diplomatic positions and calls, not domestic funding, enforcement, inspection, or measurable risk outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a78ea2bc3e660bc3","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"AIFA's 2022 financial statements showed 139 million pesos in own-service revenue against 1.282 billion pesos in federal transfers, meaning approximately 90% of total income and benefits came from government support. Own revenue did not cover its 384-million-peso payroll; the airport handled 912,415 passengers and 8,996 operations, while total liabilities rose from about 30.8 million to 371.8 million pesos during the year.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The article was published in February 2023 but reports AIFA's 2022 financial and operating results, relevant to the 2023 inherited implementation record.","ruler_attribution":"The airport was a flagship project of AMLO's administration; the supplied financial evidence concerns the institution and federal transfers rather than a personal order by AMLO.","limitations":["The source is journalistic and does not establish whether the subsidy strategy was intended as temporary or whether later 2023 performance changed."]},{"source_id":"SRC-53983362a192c509","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"An INE-published analysis argued that the proposed Plan B electoral reform would let the foreign ministry validate overseas voter information, expose voter data through politically controlled public buildings, remove the INE executive secretary outside the constitutional appointment process, expand a government-aligned internal comptroller's role into operational matters, and abolish the 300 district executive boards and their professional electoral staff. The analysis concluded these changes threatened INE autonomy and authentic elections.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.5","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published 21 February 2023 and directly concerns the administration's proposed 2023 reform.","ruler_attribution":"The analysis describes the Plan B legislation promoted by the government and approved or considered by legislators; it does not independently document AMLO's personal drafting or every legislative actor's motive.","limitations":["This is an INE-published opinion analysis by electoral counselor Ciro Murayama, not a judicial merits ruling; some claims are predictive."]},{"source_id":"SRC-238a34e18d1f9233","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"An INE-published February 2023 analysis stated that Plan B would eliminate 300 district executive boards staffed by five professionally recruited and evaluated officials, replace metropolitan coverage with inadequate single auxiliary offices, compress party-representative registration to 48 hours before voting, and remove INE assistance for transporting election packages. It warned these provisions could disrupt voter administration, invalidate polling stations, prevent timely return of packages, and create a serious political crisis.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.5","4B.10","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published 1 February 2023 and directly addresses the proposed 2023 reform.","ruler_attribution":"The source characterizes an electoral reform of the government; it does not prove AMLO personally authored each provision or that the predicted harms occurred.","limitations":["The source is an INE-published analysis and presents projected consequences rather than verified post-implementation outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d3485dd51bfe607b","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Le Monde reported that AMLO left office with more than 75% favorable opinion; it credited his administration with a doubled minimum wage, improved economic conditions for most Mexicans, and nine million people lifted from poverty. The same account said he had promised to demilitarize Mexico but instead gave the military almost full powers in security matters, leaving a more complicated security policy to his successor.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.6","3B.10","5B.8","5B.10","6B.10","8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Published 1 October 2024 and summarizes the completed 2018-2024 presidency; it is retrospective evidence about the end-state, not a contemporaneous 2023 source.","ruler_attribution":"The article directly attributes the stated promise, military-policy reversal, economic changes, and popularity to AMLO's presidency.","limitations":["The supplied excerpt is subscriber-gated and gives no detailed methodology for the poverty estimate or security assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1a26993457526634","start_unit":3,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Verificado reviewed 25 verifiable claims from AMLO's 14-18 February 2022 morning press conferences and classified 10 as false and 6 as misleading, including claims about corruption, government-business ties, public debt, impunity, repression of journalists, and INAI authority. It reported that the statements primarily defended the government and often repeated claims that did not correspond to the documented facts.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","7B.1","7B.2","7B.7","7B.8","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The evidence concerns February 2022, providing prior-period context rather than direct 2023 evidence.","ruler_attribution":"The fact-checking review directly attributes the statements to AMLO's morning conferences.","limitations":["The article does not establish whether the claims were knowingly false, whether AMLO corrected them later, or whether the pattern continued in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c61c5110cd037e24","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"After the Supreme Court granted a provisional suspension against all articles of Plan B, the INE unanimously suspended implementation in March 2023 and ordered its units to operate under the prior electoral rules. The INE stated that the decision preserved legal certainty, political-electoral and privacy rights, organizational continuity, workers' rights, and adequate citizen service pending the Court's final resolution.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.8","4B.10","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"exculpatory","period_fit":"Directly dated to March 2023 and fits the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The source documents independent INE and Supreme Court actions constraining implementation; it does not show AMLO's personal compliance beyond the institutional process.","limitations":["The excerpt does not report the later final constitutional ruling or the executive's subsequent response."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a63838848bd844aa","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"ARTICLE 19 documented 331 attacks against journalists and media in Mexico during January-June 2022, including 12 journalist murders, four internal-displacement cases, two exiles, and 128 attacks attributed to the state. It reported persistent stigmatizing discourse from the federal executive that labeled media conservative, bought, or adversarial, alongside intimidation, threats, physical attacks, illegitimate use of public power, and continuing impunity; it called for prevention, protection, justice, and access-to-information measures.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.4","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","7B.2","7B.6","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report covers the first half of 2022 and supplies prior-period context for the 2023 assessment.","ruler_attribution":"ARTICLE 19 specifically identifies stigmatizing discourse from the federal executive and attributes a substantial share of attacks to state actors, but does not attribute every attack or killing personally to AMLO.","limitations":["The report is not a 2023 measurement and does not establish the administration's response to each documented incident."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-bf3a62ad947d9a57"],"batch_limitations":["Several sources concern 2022 or earlier and therefore provide contextual rather than direct 2023 evidence.","The supplied materials often describe government or institutional conduct without proving AMLO's personal authorship, intent, knowledge, or corrective response.","No source supplied direct evidence on nuclear command-and-control, nuclear custody, nuclear proliferation enforcement, or AI/cyber safeguards beyond Mexico's diplomatic WMD and dual-use technology positions."]}
